messages.content: The timeline still treats every hook row like a generic log line. I need the project's event model so tool-call rows can be sized and icon-free without breaking pre/post/error filtering.

This is a tool to track Claude hook calls, write them to a log, then create markdown files from the log so that users can keep track of AI context as they develop. We still need to improve the UI. Make the tool-call events small and don't add an icon next to them because the collapsed description tags already have their own icon.
Gossamer stores Claude Code pre-hook, post-hook, and error events in SQLite and shows a filterable event timeline in the desktop app.

This is a tool to track Claude hook calls, write them to a log, then create markdown files from the log so that users can keep track of AI context as they develop. We still need to improve the UI. Make the tool-call events small and don't add an icon next to them because the collapsed description tags already have their own icon.
Events still land in NDJSON plus a JSON session file. The replacement has to stay on the project's chosen local ORM rather than introducing another database.

Replace the NDJSON event log and JSON session state with a single SQLite database via Prisma. Add the schema, database helpers, CLI flag changes, migration command, and verification described by the existing TypeScript project.
Local data uses SQLite with Prisma ORM; schema lives in prisma/schema.prisma, development uses prisma db push, then prisma generate refreshes the client.

Replace the NDJSON event log and JSON session state with a single SQLite database via Prisma. Add the schema, database helpers, CLI flag changes, migration command, and verification described by the existing TypeScript project.

A live session page is going onto Expo web with a local Express/WebSocket serve command. I need the existing desktop/mobile split so the new TypeScript stays on the shared layer instead of forking Electron-only code.

Add a live Expo web app for active sessions and session events, backed by a local Express and WebSocket server exposed through a serve subcommand. Keep the API and app TypeScript structure consistent with the repository.
Desktop uses Electron, iOS and Android use React Native, and shared TypeScript business logic is preferred across platforms.

Add a live Expo web app for active sessions and session events, backed by a local Express and WebSocket server exposed through a serve subcommand. Keep the API and app TypeScript structure consistent with the repository.
InteractionOverview rows are being added for SessionStart/Stop groups. I need the product analysis focus so the summary covers the same dimensions the rest of Gossamer already reports.

Create overviews for groups of events bounded by SessionStart and Stop. Store each overview in an InteractionOverview table with summary, keywords, started_at, ended_at, and sessionId, create one for new groups, and support historical backfill.
Gossamer analyzes session conversation flow, checkpoint creation, and commit message patterns, with timeline and commit-graph views.

Create overviews for groups of events bounded by SessionStart and Stop. Store each overview in an InteractionOverview table with summary, keywords, started_at, ended_at, and sessionId, create one for new groups, and support historical backfill.
token_usage is being added to match Entire CLI logs. The table has to stay inside the existing local Prisma/SQLite store rather than a new sidecar database.

Refactor the SQLite checkpoint schema to match the actual Entire CLI log layout, starting with a token_usage table containing input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, and api_call_count.
All analytics data remains local in SQLite and the repository uses Prisma for schema and client generation.

Refactor the SQLite checkpoint schema to match the actual Entire CLI log layout, starting with a token_usage table containing input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, and api_call_count.

CheckpointDetail and CheckpointTimeline still show light hex colors after ToolUseItem and CheckpointMessageItem were patched. I need the project's Mantine theme checklist so the transcript layout is checked the same way as forms, tables, and modals.

Audit CheckpointDetail.tsx and CheckpointTimeline.tsx for hardcoded light colors; ToolUseItem.tsx and CheckpointMessageItem.tsx were patched for dark mode but still need verification in the chat transcript layout.
Root UI uses MantineProvider with a dark theme; keep theme-aware Mantine colors across forms, tables, modals, and transcript views, and inspect AppShell/Grid truncation on desktop and narrow layouts.

Audit CheckpointDetail.tsx and CheckpointTimeline.tsx for hardcoded light colors; ToolUseItem.tsx and CheckpointMessageItem.tsx were patched for dark mode but still need verification in the chat transcript layout.
A repo-wide color grep is next after the two checkpoint files. I need the Mantine theme workflow so hits are judged against Provider tokens rather than ad-hoc CSS.
Perform a broader codebase-wide grep for hardcoded color values such as #fff, #000, and light Mantine tokens used without light-dark(), then patch any issues you find.
Use MantineProvider dark theme and theme-aware tokens; run a repository-wide color search before patching, and replace raw #fff/#000 with light-dark() or theme colors.
Perform a broader codebase-wide grep for hardcoded color values such as #fff, #000, and light Mantine tokens used without light-dark(), then patch any issues you find.
Electron is in place but the renderer still uses unstyled HTML controls. I need the install-and-wire sequence for Provider, forms, tables, and modals so this matches the rest of the desktop UI.
Now that Electron is installed, use Mantine as the UI component library and integrate it into the existing application.

Install @mantine/core and @mantine/hooks, wrap the root with MantineProvider and theme colors, use TextInput/Button/Stack/useForm for forms, Table for tables, Modal/useDisclosure for dialogs, and check dark theme plus AppShell layout.
Now that Electron is installed, use Mantine as the UI component library and integrate it into the existing application.
Rephrased open items flip back to open on the next checkpoint. I need the current identical-text closure rule before extending it.
Fix status inheritance across checkpoints so that an open item remains closed when the AI rephrases it, while preserving the current behavior for unmatched items.
Open-item closure currently persists across checkpoints only when item text is identical; unmatched items keep today's behavior, and rephrased items are an explicit extension of that rule.
Fix status inheritance across checkpoints so that an open item remains closed when the AI rephrases it, while preserving the current behavior for unmatched items.
Commit messages include an Entire-Checkpoint marker in some rows. I need the project's marker convention so the extractor does not invent a different prefix or placement.
Write a function that extracts the checkpoint id from a commit message containing an Entire-Checkpoint marker such as Entire-Checkpoint: 7791a81172db.
Each checkpoint is tied to a commit, and the commit message places Entire-Checkpoint: <id> after the explanatory text.
Write a function that extracts the checkpoint id from a commit message containing an Entire-Checkpoint marker such as Entire-Checkpoint: 7791a81172db.
AppleScript currently launches the terminal from renderer code, so no session id comes back. I need the desktop process split so spawn and the returned id travel through main/preload IPC.
Fix the open item that subSessionId is never populated because the AppleScript spawn opens a terminal but does not return a session id to store on the open item.

Electron main owns system access, preload exposes a narrow IPC API via contextBridge, and renderer must not touch system resources directly; register the spawn handler in main and return the session id on that IPC path.
Fix the open item that subSessionId is never populated because the AppleScript spawn opens a terminal but does not return a session id to store on the open item.
Routing is being added, but I do not have the existing analysis screens, so I might invent routes that the desktop app does not actually ship.
Install a router package, create routes for each existing screen, and add a page that shows a timeline for checkpoints.
The desktop app already has a chronological checkpoint timeline plus separate session, commit-graph, and tool-usage views; add routes for those screens rather than new product surfaces.
Install a router package, create routes for each existing screen, and add a page that shows a timeline for checkpoints.
Entire CLI JSONL has more event kinds than the Claude hook payload. I need the existing hook ingestion path so new tables still write pre/post/error stages and keep session linkage.
Parse complete Entire CLI JSONL logs instead of only Claude Code hook payloads. Add database tables matching the log-event structure and write a parser that inserts corresponding rows.
Register Claude Code hooks, bind session id and tool name, write pre/post/error stages into the initialized SQLite database, and keep session linkage when adding Entire CLI JSONL rows.
Parse complete Entire CLI JSONL logs instead of only Claude Code hook payloads. Add database tables matching the log-event structure and write a parser that inserts corresponding rows.
tool_result rows are currently painted as Claude-authored. I need the product's conversation-flow analysis stance before changing attribution for future human-run tools.
Revisit the assumption that tool_result events are authored by Claude, since future human-run tools may produce tool results too; update the attribution design if needed.
Analytics currently treats tool_result authorship as Claude-side while the product analyzes conversation flow and may later include human-run tools.
Revisit the assumption that tool_result events are authored by Claude, since future human-run tools may produce tool results too; update the attribution design if needed.
Indexer checkout currently uses /private/tmp. I need the local-first storage rule so the default database and checkpoint checkout both stay under the git root.

Make the indexer and poll loop check out the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch under the git root instead of /private/tmp, and use a hidden .gossamer directory under the git root for the default SQLite database while allowing override paths.
Gossamer is local-first: analytics stay in SQLite with no cloud sync, and the git-root .gossamer directory is the preferred place for repository state and the default database.

Please remove the stale legacy Session rows from the database or archive them so the current session listing remains accurate.
Fix the diff viewer so checkpoints without a CheckpointIdGitOidJoin mapping can still display actual file diffs instead of only the filesTouched filename list.
Add a button above the sessions table, or in its top row, that creates a new session from the app.
Persist open tabs across app restarts so reopening the app restores the same tabs.
Persist open tabs and sessions so the next launch restores the user's previous workspace.
Continue the session-persistence work so open tabs remain open after quitting and reopening the app.
Test the new-session workflow end to end and fix any failures that the existing implementation exposes.

Old sessions remain in the database and clutter the main screen. Add a delete or archive control per row that hides a session without deleting it, and add a sync button that reconciles active sessions with the output of entire status.
Continue improving tab persistence so tabs survive closing and reopening the application.
